documents.title: Math.sumPrecise()
documents.summary: The Math.sumPrecise() static method takes an iterable of numbers and returns the sum of them. It is more precise than summing them up in a loop, because it avoids floating point precision loss in intermediate results.

body: Because <mark>sumPrecise</mark>() is a static method of <mark>Math</mark>, you always use it as <mark>Math</mark>.sumPrecise(), rather than as a method of a <mark>Math</mark>
object you created (<mark>Math</mark> is not a constructor).
title: <mark>Math</mark>.sumPrecise()

documents.title: Math.random()
documents.summary: The Math.random() static method returns a floating-point, pseudo-random number that's greater than or equal to 0 and less than 1, with approximately uniform distribution over that range — which you can then scale to your desired range. The implementation selects the initial seed to the random number generation algorithm; it cannot be chosen or reset by the user.
